Frank — great questions. Short answers below, Laura and Vivek added technical notes in a follow-up: 

1) Per-node GPU options: we validate for A100 40GB and H100 80GB profiles. For 4k max tokens and heavy KV cache workloads we recommend H100-class nodes for sustained throughput; per-node memory footprint (KV + model) estimates are in the attached spec (see section 2.3). If you want we can run a quick perf sim with your typical prompt distribution.

2) Model/quantization upgrades in air-gapped envs: we support signed artifacts that can be transferred via removable media. Our release package includes a signed manifest and verification tool; Redwood engineers can provide an offline signing key handshake during onboarding.

3) Backup rotation & restore tests: typical model is collaborative — LegacyBank owns operational backups and retention (per your policies) and we provide runbooks and one-time assistance during the initial 90-day rollout for restore drills. Ongoing restore SLA support is available as a paid add-on.

Attached a small matrix with the quick mapping to your procurement checklist. Let us know a good time next week for a 30-min technical validation (virtual) — propose Tue 11/7 10:00 or Wed 11/8 14:00 PT.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Frank — Laura from Solutions here; short technical notes to supplement Marissa: 

- KV cache sizing: the spec uses conservative estimates (1.8x multiplier on peak seq length). If you provide a sample of your prompt length distribution (even anonymized), we can tighten the per-node memory requirement and give expected throughput/TPS.
- Firmware/driver upgrades: on-centers we recommend staging nodes in a maintenance ring (2 nodes) to validate upgrades before full deployment; offline installers we provide include checksums and a verification utility.
- Networking: for pure airgap installs you still need a secure jump host for initial provisioning (temporary, can be removed post-provision). Our template includes the minimal ports and DNS exceptions needed for internal orchestration only.

I'll bring a short checklist to the tech validation call so we can walk through your network diagram live.

-Laura
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Frank / Priya — Vivek from Security. A couple notes on the airgap operational playbook and a proposed model for upgrade verification: 

- Signing & verification: we will provide a signed artifact payload and a small verification binary (no external calls) that validates manifests using your HSM or a short-lived onboarding key. We never ship private model weights to public endpoints.
- Upgrade approvals: propose a two-step approval for production changes: (1) staging validation (runbook-driven) and (2) engineering approval sign-off (audit trail preserved in the runbook).
- Offline incident response: include a periodic restore test every quarter and an annual forensic snapshot; we can include templates in the offline-ops-checklist.

If you want a written statement about our artifact signing process for your procurement/security packet, I can draft that and attach it to the HubSpot record.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Security Architect
Redwood Inference
